target: modal top layer and document inertness
observed_behavior: The HTML Standard defines a document as blocked by the topmost dialog in that document's top layer. While blocked, connected nodes outside that subject dialog and its flat-tree descendants become inert; showModal() causes the relevant top-layer mechanism. The dialog itself escapes inertness inherited from ancestors, but can become inert if its own inert attribute is specified, and descendants may be independently inert.
context: W07 B2 K3 read-only observation; WHATWG HTML Living Standard authoritative for the described native HTML mechanisms and guarded algorithms only; source shows Last Updated 20 July 2026.
limitations: Document blocking is tied to the topmost modal dialog in the top layer, not to any CSS backdrop or visually prominent overlay.
The subject and its flat-tree descendants are excluded from automatic surrounding-document inertness, subject to separately specified inertness.
Multiple modal dialogs, other top-layer members, and the user's context cannot be reduced to a universal z-index or library stacking rule.
No live pointer, keyboard, modal layering or accessibility technology was tested.
